design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 (condo_coverage_changes)

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 4]. Root condo_ext_unit_rental_charge takes 5 factors, prerequisite condo_ext_liability_raise_charge takes 4.

[Why a good test] The customer asks only to have her condo set up for renting it to a tenant. The desk must (a) read in the rental policy that the endorsement is not recorded until the declarations carry the higher of the tier's two personal liability limits, see on the policy record that the limit is 300000.00 (Special Enhanced options 300000/500000), and work out that the only write that brings the higher limit about is the liability raise; (b) price that raise from the tenure (125 months), the medical-payments history, the HomeGuard household record and the billing plan; (c) hand the customer her own rental endorsement priced on the world after the raise (landlord liability load 14.00 now in), with the companion-residence, loss-history, returning-landlord and payment-history multipliers and the earning method. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reading five record sets and arithmetic, not from tool guessing: there is exactly one tool per problem.

[Scope] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed: condo_ext_liability_raise_charge + raise_liability_limit_70984c5d (agent), condo_ext_unit_rental_charge + add_unit_rental_endorsement_60a857ee (user). Left for task 1 (its draw: 1 prerequisite, factors [5,4]): the Coverage A realignment after a master-policy change and the deductible raise credit, disjoint policies and tools.

[Problem-tree card] root condo_ext_unit_rental_charge (user tool). Edge root -> condo_ext_liability_raise_charge: kind value_input, gate landlord_liability_load, form state, policy_source "A unit rental endorsement is not recorded until the declarations carry the higher of the tier's two personal liability limits." (negated direction: a booking is not made until what it waits for stands), condition condo_policies.liability_limit = higher tier option, resolved_by raise_liability_limit_70984c5d (agent). Four-point test: ordering connective "not ... until"; waits on a record-visible state (liability limit on the declarations); names no tool/id/code token; hard requirement at the exact scope (the higher of the tier's two limits). Only one write of this difficulty sets condo_policies.liability_limit (the liability raise tool), so the state form resolves to one action. Derivation: sentence + record 300000.00 + liability rule ("A liability raise moves the personal liability limit ... from the lower to the higher ...") -> the liability raise. False at opening: initial_state.condo_policies.5112e9b4-a527-47ce-9473-58dede5b337a.liability_limit = 300000.0. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): without the raise the rental prorated_premium is 40.40 instead of 47.84 and the liability endorsement/billing rows are missing. Topological order: liability raise (step 8) then rental (step 10). user_scenario names neither the liability limit nor the raise; the tools validate nothing (they write as passed).

[Base-invariant card] Subjects condo_endorsement_added / condo_coverage_updated / condo_additional_premium. condo_endorsements.endorsable_status: status in_force (initial_state.condo_policies.5112e9b4-a527-47ce-9473-58dede5b337a.status). condo_endorsements.open_claim_freeze: both claims closed (d6797fea-d62c-44fe-94fe-ee3b924bbeac, df677b31-c0d7-49c3-93e2-b7188169f192), no open claim. condo_endorsements.no_backdated_change: retired by the declared overwrite in both policies ("... takes effect on the day the named insured requests it, and that day is before the expiration date"), which pins the effective date to 2026-09-24 < 2027-04-15; the tools write request_date = effective_date = ctx.now() date. condo_association_changes / condo_cancellation_and_reinstatement: policy_scope (no association change on record, no cancellation). Base unit_rental availability: unit_rental_allowed is true on Special Enhanced. No time eligibility applies to these subjects, so temporal_feasibility is [].

[Business-object card] Target: CondoGuard policy CG6-3187-5520 (condo_policy_id 5112e9b4-a527-47ce-9473-58dede5b337a) of customer Delphine Achterberg-Moyo; both writes attach to it. Rows aggregated: claim payments f78f1511-2f64-4597-bbc2-f33fb5b6394e (medical payments, 2023-12-20) and a43c8feb-e3e5-4af6-a044-a31e44f30ee0 (unit property, 2024-11-26); endorsements 51342053-0dc5-4349-8e76-5cea28531ada/876a1645-a353-4c1a-9801-5b81e0307077 (earlier rental); billing 35d1caf5-c9db-4d53-b258-927ca896ae77,08ff4660-2cb7-48b9-b086-bf5f12830b88 (billed installments of the 2026-04-15 term), f8ff551f-94c2-4232-8d0d-75fc68dfc13a (late fee 2026-07-26); HomeGuard 95feda72-5c99-4a88-b63a-ab89d5326017. Excluded: a43c8feb-e3e5-4af6-a044-a31e44f30ee0 from the liability loss count (not a liability/medical-payments part); the installment fee 028fa5ce-3709-4b46-81aa-9c9f649e9b5f and payments 2070edbb-236b-4de5-a22e-561722b21f69,cb8870a7-0384-47b9-be42-1ee5cbcd5bd4 from the installment count (not premium installments); the late fee from the fully-earned test (not a returned payment).

[Factor card] Liability charge (base 14.00 x 1 step, calendar-day share 203/365 -> baseline 7.79): liability_tenure 125 months -> 0.85 (alone at baseline 7.00); liability_loss_load one medical payment within 60 months -> 1.25 (4.76); household_liability HomeGuard in force, liability 500000 -> 0.80 (7.44), cross-difficulty home; liability_billing_share quarterly 2/4 unbilled -> 0.5 (6.62). Gold 5.95. Rental charge (base (76.00+14.00) x 203/365 -> baseline 50.05): companion_residence HomeGuard primary residence AND 125 >= 60 months -> 0.90 (53.16), multi-source + cross-difficulty home; rental_loss_history two payments in 36 months -> 1.25 (38.28); returning_landlord earlier rental 26 >= 24 months -> 0.90 (53.16); rental_payment_history late fee within 12 months -> 1.05 (45.57); rental_earning no returned payment, quarterly 2/4 unbilled -> 0.5 (53.21). Gold 47.84. Near-misses: the unit-property payment for the liability loss load; the late fee for the fully-earned tier. No outcome stamp exists in the schema for any factor.

[Seed rationale] customers row (identity + locator); condo policy (tier, limits, dates, plan, balance 0.00 = current-term ledger); 6 current-term billing rows (installments 1-2, installment fee, late fee, two card payments; installments 3-4 not billed); 2 endorsement rows (2019 rental added, 2021 removed); 6 claim rows (two closed claims); one HomeGuard policy (new house, in force since 2026-08-28, primary, liability 500000). Removing any of: the late fee (payment multiplier -> 0.97), a claim payment (loss multipliers move), the rental history (landlord multiplier -> 1.00), the HomeGuard row (both cross multipliers -> 1.00), a billed installment (shares move) changes a scored figure. No base automatic clause fires: every billed installment is paid, no nonpayment notice is owed, claims are closed, and renewal is months away. No cache field is used as a difficulty.

[Persona design] Delphine, rushed after a move, volunteers only the goal (condo set up for the unit rented to a tenant from October 1, in place today), the fact she moved into a Rocky River house, and that she will sign the rental coverage herself. Credentials (DOB 1983-11-06, ZIP 44116), policy number, HomeGuard number, earlier rental and the lease type come only when asked. Passive reactions: if told another change must come first she lets the desk make it; she runs the handed-over tool with the figures read to her; she closes when told the rental coverage is on. She never names the liability limit, never gives a figure, never corrects.

[Reachability] Every read is a share lookup keyed by the customer id or policy id; the liability limit value comes from the tier table in the KB; the policy id from the lookup; both computed figures from the published rules and the rows read. Everything lands under one frozen_time (2026-09-24); no waiting, visit, payment clearing or review is involved.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(DOB, ZIP) -> read condo policy, endorsements, claims, billing, HomeGuard -> unlock + call raise_liability_limit_70984c5d(condo_policy_id, 500000.0, 11.9, 5.95) -> unlock user tool and hand over -> customer calls add_unit_rental_endorsement_60a857ee(condo_policy_id, 95.68, 47.84).

[Verification run] scratchpad authoring script evaluating extended compute on the handling-time world (real tools replayed): LIAB result 5.95, factor baselines 7.0/4.76/7.44/6.62, all-baseline 7.79; RENT result 47.84 (after step 8), factor baselines 53.16/38.28/53.16/45.57/53.21, all-baseline 50.05, without the liability raise 40.40. Gates run: check_extended/check_task_tools/replay_tasks/check_solvability/check_compute/check_grounding/check_cross_fire --task 0 all OK.

[Two-way rule/compute sweep] Every world-reading or choosing binding quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis (tenure, loss counts with windows and coverage parts, HomeGuard status/limit/occupancy, installment count keyed to the current term's effective date, share methods, one-step raise, multiplier combination 'first multiplied together and then applied once', rounding 'full-year figure rounded first and the share applied to the rounded figure'). Reverse: each quantity/window/branch/rounding sentence of both rules is claimed by a binding; no filter exists in compute that the rule lacks.

[Solvability vs GT] step 8: endorsable_status and open_claim_freeze evidenced by initial_state rows bound to condo_policy_id; step 10 additionally cites prior_step:8 for the stage fact. Draft recomputation from visible context (rules, schemas, lookups, persona) gives the same two writes, the same order and the same figures; the only non-computed numeric argument, 500000.0, is fixed by the tier table.

[Revisions]
- Audit round 1, F0-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED). Symptom: factor_sensitivity for rental_loss_history and rental_payment_history declared 38.27 and 45.56; exact half-up gives 38.28 and 45.57. Root cause: both substitutions land on exact half-cent ties (76.545 -> 38.275; 91.125 -> 45.565) and the compute used binary-float rounding (round-half-even on an inexact float) while the rule says half-up. Change: every rounding binding of all four extended policies now computes int(round(x * 100, 6) + 0.5) / 100, which is exact half-up on these positive figures; each rule gained the sentence '... is half-up in exact decimal: a figure lying exactly halfway between two cents goes to the higher cent', quoted in the result basis. Re-run: rental_loss_history 38.28, rental_payment_history 45.57; every gold figure (5.95, 11.90, 47.84, 95.68) and every other proof figure unchanged; propagated to computations[1].factor_sensitivity, factor_trace, evaluation_criteria[10] tracing and this dossier.
- Audit observation (home row): Coverage C on HG3-3906-4417 changed from 206000.00 to 289000.00 = HO-3 Premier personal_property_pct 70 of Coverage A 412000.00, rounded up to the next 1,000 (home charter default); no factor reads it, no figure moves.
- Audit observations O-3 (tool docstrings said 'Afterwards'): reworded to 'On success the declarations show ...'. O-6 (the value the liability raise feeds into the rental is the tier's step premium, switched on by the higher limit): kept by design; the rule charges the landlord load at the tier's liability step premium for the higher limit, the edge bears weight on this world (40.40 -> 47.84), and the prerequisite sentence and the load sentence each state their own rule. O-4 (no 'none' path below the minimum premium change): no gold charge of this task is below 5.00 (5.95, 47.84), so the inherited clause never bites here; noted for later tasks. O-2/O-5 (plan-dependent share methods, installment/month earning): each method is stated in full in its own policy and owned by one quantity; kept.
user_scenario:
You are Delphine Achterberg-Moyo, a hospital pharmacist in her early forties who talks quickly and a little apologetically, the way someone does who has been living out of moving boxes for a month. You call Larkspur Mutual from your phone, 419-362-7148, which is the number on your profile. Late in August you moved out of your condominium at Edgewater Terrace in Lakewood and into a house you bought in Rocky River, and you have signed a one-year lease with a tenant who moves into the condo on October 1. What you want from this call is simple: you want your condo insurance set up for the unit being rented out to that tenant, and you want it in place as of today so you are covered before the tenant arrives. You understand there will be an extra charge and you are fine paying it; you just want it done correctly on this call. You would rather the representative handle whatever they can on their end, but if the rental coverage itself is something you have to agree to or sign yourself, you will do that part yourself right now on the call.
You give your phone number when you first explain who you are. You do not recite anything else up front. If the representative asks you to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, 1983-11-06, and the ZIP code of your mailing address, 44116, which is the new house; your mailing address there is 3318 Wyandotte Ridge Road, Rocky River, OH 44116, and you give it only if asked. If asked for the condo policy number you read it off an old declarations page: CG6-3187-5520. The condo is Unit 7B at 1450 Edgewater Terrace, Lakewood, OH 44107, in the Edgewater Terrace Condominium Association. If asked whether you have other Larkspur policies, you say yes, you insured the new house with HomeGuard when you bought it, and you live there now; you give that policy number, HG3-3906-4417, only if asked for it. If asked whether you have rented the condo out before, you say you did once, for a couple of years around 2019 to 2021, and then moved back in. If asked what kind of rental this is, it is a standard one-year lease to one tenant, not a short-term or vacation rental. You do not remember what you pay for the condo policy and you do not know what the rental coverage costs; if the representative wants a figure from you, you say you would rather they look it up.
If the representative tells you that something else on the condo policy has to be changed before the rental coverage can go on, you ask what it is, listen, and then tell them to go ahead and make that change on your policy today; you do not argue about it or ask for anything extra. Once the representative tells you the rental endorsement is ready for you and gives you what you need to put it through, you do it yourself exactly as they describe, using the policy reference and the figures they read out to you, and you tell them what confirmation you got back. When you hear that the rental coverage is on the policy and what it adds to your bill, you thank them, say that is all you needed, and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Gives the tier (unit rental allowed; liability options 300000/500000; step premium 14.00; rental premium 76.00), the declared liability limit that makes the rental prerequisite false (the rental is not recorded until the declarations carry the higher liability limit), the tenure evidence of the tenure and companion-residence multipliers, and the billing plan/term dates the billing-share methods read.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Evidence of the liability loss multiplier (one medical payments payment within 60 months), the rental loss-history multiplier (two claim payments within 36 months), and of the open-claim freeze gate (both claims closed, no open claim).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the premium account of the current term: installments 1 and 2 billed (4 quarterly installments), an installment fee, a late fee posted 2026-07-26, two card payments, no returned payment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Evidence of the billing-share methods (2 of 4 installments unbilled; no returned payment so the rental is not fully earned) and of the rental payment-history multiplier (one late fee within 12 months).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the liability raise tool so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the prerequisite problem; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Resolves the prerequisite of the rental endorsement (the rental is not recorded until the declarations carry the higher of the tier's liability limits); condo_ext_liability_raise_charge computes prorated_premium.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.condo_policy_id: (1) 5112e9b4-a527-47ce-9473-58dede5b337a. (2) Basis: the raise_liability_limit docstring 'the reference number of the CondoGuard policy being endorsed, as returned by the condo policy lookup for the verified customer'; the lookup at step 2 returns exactly one CondoGuard policy for this customer (initial_state.condo_policies.5112e9b4-a527-47ce-9473-58dede5b337a). (3) Unique: the customer holds one condo policy; no other id is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.liability_limit: (1) 500000.0. (2) Basis: rule 'A liability raise moves the personal liability limit on a CondoGuard policy from the lower to the higher of the two personal liability limits the tier offers' and the Special Enhanced tier's liability options [300000, 500000]; the rental rule 'A unit rental endorsement is not recorded until the declarations carry the higher of the tier's two personal liability limits.' (3) Unique: the tier has exactly two options and the declarations carry the lower (300000.00), so the only raise is to 500000.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.annual_premium_change: (1) 11.9. Computed intermediate of condo_ext_liability_raise_charge: tier liability step premium 14.00 x tenure multiplier 0.85 (125 whole months since 2016-04-15, tier >=120) x liability loss multiplier 1.25 (one medical payments payment, CGC-23-318406 on 2023-12-20, within 60 months; the 2024 unit-property payment is not a liability/medical payment) x household multiplier 0.80 (HomeGuard HG3-3906-4417 in force, liability 500000.00) = 11.90 for one step, rounded half-up to the cent. (2) Basis: 'The standard full-year liability step charge is the tier's liability step premium for each step raised, rounded half-up to the cent.' and 'The liability step premium is adjusted by three multipliers that are first multiplied together and then applied once...'. (3) Unique: every multiplier's tier is fixed by the records read at steps 2, 4, 6.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.prorated_premium: (1) 5.95. Full-year liability step charge 11.90 x liability share 0.5 (quarterly plan, installments 1 and 2 of the 2026-04-15 term billed, 2 of 4 unbilled) = 5.95, rounded half-up to the cent. Factor by factor: tenure 0.85 (baseline 1.00 -> 7.00); liability loss 1.25 (baseline 1.00 -> 4.76); household 0.80 (baseline 1.00 -> 7.44); billing share 2/4 (baseline calendar days 203/365 -> 6.62). All baselines at once -> 7.79. Any agent reading the tier table, the claims, the premium account and the HomeGuard record converges on 5.95.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the customer's own unit rental endorsement tool and hand it to her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The unit rental endorsement is the named insured's signed election; the agent unlocks it for her at its place after the liability raise.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The customer declares the unit rented to others and signs the unit rental endorsement effective today with the quoted figures.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Root problem: condo_ext_unit_rental_charge computes prorated_premium on the world after the liability raise.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.condo_policy_id: (1) 5112e9b4-a527-47ce-9473-58dede5b337a. (2) Basis: the add_unit_rental_endorsement docstring 'the reference number of the insured's own CondoGuard policy, as the service representative reads it out from the policy record'; the agent reads it from the lookup at step 2. (3) Unique: the customer's only condo policy.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.annual_premium_change: (1) 95.68. Computed intermediate of condo_ext_unit_rental_charge on the world after step 8: (tier unit rental annual premium 76.00 + landlord liability load 14.00, since the declarations now carry 500000.00) x companion residence 0.90 (HomeGuard in force insuring her primary residence, condo in force 125 >= 60 months) x rental loss-history 1.25 (two claim payments within 36 months: 2023-12-20 and 2024-11-26) x returning-landlord 0.90 (rental added 2019-06-01, removed 2021-08-01: 26 >= 24 whole months) x rental payment-history 1.05 (late fee posted 2026-07-26 within 12 months) = 95.68125, rounded half-up to 95.68. (2) Basis: 'Four rental multipliers adjust the sum of the unit rental annual premium and the landlord liability load: they are first multiplied together and then applied once to that sum, before the full-year rental charge is rounded'. (3) Unique: every tier is fixed by the records.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.prorated_premium: (1) 47.84. Full-year rental charge 95.68 x rental share 0.5 (no returned payment within 12 months; quarterly plan with 2 of 4 installments of the current term unbilled) = 47.84. Factor by factor (baseline figure when that factor alone falls back): companion 0.90 (->53.16), loss-history 1.25 (->38.28), returning-landlord 0.90 (->53.16), payment-history 1.05 (->45.57), earning method 2/4 (-> calendar days 203/365 -> 53.21); every factor at baseline -> 50.05. Without the liability raise the landlord liability load is 0 and the figure would be 40.40.

edges.policy_source: A unit rental endorsement is not recorded until the declarations carry the higher of the tier's two personal liability limits.
